💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco announced in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening.
  • It has been revealed that the press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year.
  • Recent findings suggest that bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now.

Sources indicate that as another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco announced in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. In its notice, Bandai Namco explains that the reason for the liquidation is due to Reflector not meeting its expectations for "future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation.".

It has been revealed that the press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year. This is not the first time Reflector has been cut by Bandai, as around a month after the launch of Unknown 9: Awakening and presumably in response to its low sales, 18% of the workforce was laid off. 2025 then saw further redundancies amidst the cancellation of a prospective project, though details on those layoffs were not granted by the organization. Unknown 9 was intended to be a transmedia franchise involving the game as well as comic books and novels, but these ambitions never came to pass.

Recent findings suggest that bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now. A similar process faces Arkane Lyon, which is presently in a purgatory of having been chosen for closure by Microsoft, but temporarily protected by French labor laws that prevent it from being suddenly closed without proper negotiation and procedure.

Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.
  • Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.
  • In the first case, at least, something is being done.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

In a recent development, developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”.

Today’s enhancement follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest upgrade only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

According to recent reports, the most crucial changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

In a recent development, if you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added fresh pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

Why Do I Want To Paint The Walls In Grand Theft Auto VI?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (544 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I admire the cozy sim genre.
  • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics.
  • And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I admire the cozy sim genre. Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are on regular rotation in my home on my family’s screens, but not my own. In an odd way, I find the genre stressful, arguably the opposite of its intended purpose. I will happily and cathartically guide Grace Ashcroft through the tense hallways of Rhodes Hill in Resident Evil Requiem, but Pokémon Pokopia’s seemingly endless list of to-dos makes me sweat. It’s just not my genre, and I have come to terms with that.

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics. Bird (and animal) watching, for example, is apparent and encouraged early in the experience. You can also fix up your somewhat dilapidated home from almost the moment you are let loose outside of the opening tutorial missions.

And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.

Recent findings suggest that I climbed to the roof to fix the leak and replaced all the stairs leading up to the home before I ever participated in the game’s namesake and stole a car. Normally, it’s the kind of interaction I skip or choose not to engage with, given the option. Or, I do the bare minimum to progress. Sure, I have all the options in the world to build and decorate a house and make it my own, but… that feels like a lot of work. And I am not an artist.

Sources indicate that the “cozy” elements of Grand Theft Auto VI are admittedly different from those in a game like Pokopia or Animal Crossing. You’re not designing your home (though you can pick a paint color), but it feels similar, and I am trying to figure out why I enjoy it here as opposed to other games. Is it because Jason and Lucia are so instantly believable as human beings that I want their home to be nicer?

After some thought, I think it might just come down to Grand Theft Auto VI’s consistently impressive visual fidelity. Replacing the shingles on the roof, for example, offers a close-up look at Jason’s character model, and you can practically feel the texture of the asphalt while the heat of the sun beats down.

Industry observers note that I don’t have confirmation, but it also just feels like someone at Rockstar did exhaustive research on what the process of replacing a roof shingle should look like, even if, I’m sure, it probably doesn’t quite work that way in the real world. Jason makes it look incredibly easy, to the point that it had me questioning if I should be climbing up to my own roof and taking care of some loose shingles myself. And you know what is a lot of fun? Watching someone who is good at something do the thing they’re good at.

I’m now into the driving and shooting part of the game (and enjoying that, too!), but I am shocked at how grateful I was to have the option to stay home and put up drywall.

GTA 6 Made 2 Million XBOX Players Lie About Their Nationality

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals, which might explain why millions of XBOX players technically broke their terms of service and lied about their nationality, all just to play the game a little earlier.
  • It has been revealed that there’s no denying that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of 2026, selling millions of copies ahead of launch, and quickly becoming tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, matched only by the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64.
  • It turns out that millions of XBOX players jumped the queue and decided to lie to boot up Grand Theft Auto 6 early.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals, which might explain why millions of XBOX players technically broke their terms of service and lied about their nationality, all just to play the game a little earlier.

It has been revealed that there’s no denying that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of 2026, selling millions of copies ahead of launch, and quickly becoming tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, matched only by the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. As such, millions of people were waiting at midnight on November 19, when the game became available in their region.

In a recent development, or not. It turns out that millions of XBOX players jumped the queue and decided to lie to boot up Grand Theft Auto 6 early. This is thanks to a trick that’s much easier to pull off on XBOX than PlayStation 5, prompting lots of people to change their nationality.

A report by Ampere Analysis (with thanks to Eurogamer) has revealed that over two million XBOX players used the “Fresh Zealand trick” to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early. 100,000 PlayStation 5 people did something similar, but that method was more difficult, which is why the number is much smaller.

Recent findings suggest that the Latest Zealand trick has been used for many big releases on XBOX systems in the past. Because of time zone differences, most video games launch in New Zealand first. If a player changes their XBOX system settings to New Zealand, then they can access the country’s version of the Microsoft Store, and in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, they were able to play it over twelve hours earlier.

According to recent reports, the PlayStation 5 version of the trick involves creating a separate account with billing information, which is a massive pain in the neck, which explains why only 100,000 people bothered. The New Zealand XBOX trick literally takes a minute to pull off and is easy to revert afterward.

If a player changes their XBOX system settings to New Zealand, then they can access the country’s version of the Microsoft Store, and in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, they were able to play it over twelve hours earlier.

Some fans were concerned that Microsoft would ban accounts that did the New Zealand trick. After all, it breaks the Microsoft Store's terms of service. However, many official XBOX social media accounts playfully encouraged people to do it, as it was essentially a free win for the brand, at a time when it badly needed one. As it stands, there are reports of bans, even now that the trick isn’t necessary, so there's no need for anyone to worry about switching flags.

Sources indicate that while the New Zealand trick is well-known among fans, and is something many gaming outlets will gleefully inform the public about ahead of a significant release, it’s usually only done by a small audience. Grand Theft Auto 6 is such a massive game that more people than usual temporarily became Kiwis, giving them an early chance to play.

According to recent reports, now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, it’s unclear what the next massive game will have a similar effect. 2027 has some massive hits, but it would be hard to claim any will be as notable as Grand Theft Auto VI. If Persona 6 manages to launch in 2027, then the JRPG audience on XBOX might all take a journey to Mordor, but it’ll be unlikely that millions will do so.

Company of Heroes 3 developer admits "it was a lot" to make the 3.0 overhaul patch alongside regular updates, singleplayer DLC, and a whole spinoff game

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Company of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge.
  • Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.
  • Sources indicate that the team began planning the 3.0 update two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Company of Heroes 3, and focus on challenges players had flagged since launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Company of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with upcoming autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.

Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.

Sources indicate that the team began planning the 3.0 update two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Company of Heroes 3, and focus on challenges players had flagged since launch. "The VFX were called out," executive producer Denise Christie tells me. "Same thing with a lot of our audio.".

Relic were already releasing patches every three months, but the changes they were looking at were much too large for those smaller updates. If they had tried to do the work as part of the small updates, approaching the problems with piecemeal solutions, it would have turned Organization of Heroes 3 into a hodgepodge of new and old assets. "We wanted to make sure it was a cohesive package," principal designer Eric Wrobel states. "If you increase the quality of one thing, you have to do it equally across so much stuff." Otherwise you end up with "One that looks awesome and one that's like, 'Oh, this one's kind of gross'.".

Complicating matters, though, was that the team couldn't down tools and focus on just these large changes. As well as the small patches that were still going out every three months, both the VFX and audio teams were also contributing the battlegroup DLC packs which added fresh units to the game. "They would work on stuff and in one branch that was the 3.0 work and then they would go ahead and do some battlegroup stuff and come back to that," Christie says. "It was a lot.".

As the 3.0 upgrade grew in scope, it also meant other departments were contributing to the anniversary release while working on the smaller updates and DLC. "For us to create future maps for Firm of Heroes 3, we were going to have an glitch that our assets were getting stale," Christie explains. So, as part of 3.0, Relic's art department created autumn and winter asset packs, as well as a new Industrial theme. This then created more work for the VFX team, who have added rain and snow, as well as a transition effect showing soil and concrete moving from dry to wet.

Not to be outdone, the design team also made significant changes to the singleplayer Italy campaign. The towns that dot the dynamic grand strategy-inspired map now have individual upgrades, making for more meaningful decisions when it comes to which settlement you capture next. And, responding to one of the main criticisms of Firm of Heroes 3's singleplayer, they also updated the computer's AI so it makes smarter decisions in both the turn-based and real-time battles. "We wanted to get this feel like there was that sort of back and forth of the AI resisting you and pushing forward into your territory and actually taking your stuff, which wasn't really happening in any of the previous updates," Wrobel indicates.

Further complicating matters was the fact that alongside these regular updates, the DLC, and the substantial 3.0 update release work, was that Relic also released Final Stand in July, a roguelike horde mode spinoff of Organization of Heroes 3. "We had to be very careful not to accidentally introduce this 3.0 work that was also happening at the same time," Christie notes." The improvements in this update have also rolled out for the spinoff, too.

Naturally, Relic aren't doing all this work purely out of the goodness of the hearts. The regular updates keep players engaged, Christie explains, and "hopefully bring back lapsed players who were frustrated by some of these things." It's something the team have already seen happen before, Wrobel explains. "We saw with the 2.0 enhancement that we had a big spike of customers and that was great, but because that improved the overall quality of the game, we saw each month we were selling more copies than we were before. People have been buying these games for years and years and years, so if we invest in this now we're going to see returns for quite a long time into the future as well.".

"If we were starting to see that tail down then we probably would have made a very different decision to be honest, but that's not what we see," Christie adds.

Recent findings suggest that the next release for Organization of Heroes 3 is a singleplayer DLC, Operation Torch, due out on November 25th. (So, if you're keeping count, that was also in the works while the upgrade, battlegroup DLC, and spinoff were all being made.) Until now, Relic's additions to the RTS have been focused on the multiplayer community, adding new units to be used online or in offline skirmishes. Operation Torch brings new scripted missions that trace a set of soldiers moving through North Africa.

It has been revealed that after that, though, I ask if Relic looks to continue adding to Company of Heroes 3 or if they're ready to move onto a upcoming project. "Well, it's both actually," CEO Justin Dowdeswell tells me. "We would love to continue with Company of Heroes 3 and not solely as a place for us to experiment. That's one of the advantages of being smaller, and being able to make decisions. We're not going to leave Company of Heroes 3. It's an and function. We are going to embark on the next thing.".

So, it doesn't sound like Relic are taking anything off their plate….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, one of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the newly introduced Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the significant news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

In a recent development, first off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

Industry observers note that GSC Game World states Cost of Hope will introduce two upcoming regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Sources indicate that each of the two upcoming regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

According to recent reports, the developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

Tech Report: Grand Theft Auto VI's Auto Drive Is A Beautiful And Free Version Of Hands-Free Travel

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel.
  • It let's the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky having to pay attention to the road.
  • In a recent development, first, you must select a destination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

This is where Auto Drive comes in. It let's the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky having to pay attention to the road. Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

In a recent development, first, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

Next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

Sources indicate that once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back make and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, lead writer of the hit 2025 RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has revealed that she is no longer with developer Sandfall Interactive.
  • Recent findings suggest that clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was universally acclaimed and won an astounding list of awards, including just about every narrative-focused prize you can name: Best Storytelling at the Golden Joysticks, Best Narrative at The Game Awards, Outstanding Achievement in Story at DICE, Best Narrative at the GDC Awards, Best Narrative at the BAFTAs, and Hugo and Nebula awards.
  • Recent findings suggest that despite Clair Obscur's success, Svedberg-Yen revealed that she moved on from the game, and the studio, earlier this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, lead writer of the hit 2025 RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has revealed that she is no longer with developer Sandfall Interactive. In an interview with Gamesbeat, Svedberg-Yen said she wants to return to her own creative efforts, including stories for film and television, and also aims to set up a new fund specifically to support the advancement of narrative design in games.

Recent findings suggest that clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was universally acclaimed and won an astounding list of awards, including just about every narrative-focused prize you can name: Best Storytelling at the Golden Joysticks, Best Narrative at The Game Awards, Outstanding Achievement in Story at DICE, Best Narrative at the GDC Awards, Best Narrative at the BAFTAs, and Hugo and Nebula awards. That makes it particularly interesting that Clair Obscur is Svedberg-Yen's one and only game credit: Prior to joining Sandfall Interactive in 2020 as one of its earliest members, she spent years working in the finance industry.

Recent findings suggest that despite Clair Obscur's success, Svedberg-Yen revealed that she moved on from the game, and the studio, earlier this year. "I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she noted. "We’ve parted ways.".

That has to hurt for Sandfall, but Svedberg-Yen still has ambitions within the game industry, including the creation of an investment fund for "narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers.".

Industry observers note that "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face," Svedberg-Yen stated. "To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.

Sources indicate that "In that way I can also help them build a stronger narrative foundation from the beginning. I’ve done a lot of consulting work with different studios. I’ve discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it’s a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.".

Svedberg-Yen said a lot of studios think of narrative as "a skin," something thrown on near the end of the development process once everything else is assembled. But that's like trying to solve a puzzle without knowing whether there's actually a solution at all, she continued, "whereas if you start from the very beginning, when everyone is starting from the same jumping-off point, everything will naturally be able to tie together.".

The goal is not to compete with publishers, she explained, but "to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make.".

Recent findings suggest that that investment fund, alongside her own projects and stories, will be Svedberg-Yen's primary focus in the coming year: "The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help. That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter.
  • Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games.
  • According to recent reports, alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

According to recent reports, alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

In a recent development, sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

The wait between Persona 5 and Persona 6 has been a long one. In September, Persona 5 turned 10, and while we've had our first teaser for Persona 6, it's likely to hit the 11-year mark before we actually see it. There has been enough to keep hardcore series fans happy during that time, with multiple spin-offs as well as remakes of Persona 3 and, soon, Persona 4, but it's been agonizing.

Thankfully, Atlus seems fully aware of this problem and has pledged that it is "working on various things" to make sure we don't have to wait anywhere near as long for the next entry of its beloved JRPG series.

Industry observers note that 11 years is a long time to wait for any sequel; just ask Grand Theft Auto 6 fans, who are now diving into the game after a 13-year wait. For context, there were three years between Persona (which is reportedly also getting the remake treatment) and Persona 2, seven years between Persona 2 and Persona 3, just two between 3 and 4, and then eight between Persona 4 and Persona 5. The long wait for Persona 6 is now finally coming to an end.

The eight years between Persona 4 and Persona 5 were already killer, but 11 is taking things to the next level. It won't be the case for the next entry, though, if Atlus is to be believed.

In a new interview, posted today on the official Sega website, Persona series producer Kazuhisa Wada discussed the future of the franchise, including the work on Persona 6 and beyond.

In a recent development, "The one we're right now working on is Persona 6. While there's still limited information I can share, we want to prove the results of all the challenges we've faced so far through the game itself. With that in mind, we're creating something even better than before, and we're feeling a real sense of accomplishment as we work on it," he said. His following comments were the most interesting, though.

It has been revealed that "And Persona 6 is not the end. We are working on various things to ensure that you don't have to wait as long for the next installment as we have in the past. And in order to make Persona an even bigger IP, we are constantly thinking about creative ideas and developments that will not disappoint your expectations. Please look forward to what's to come from Persona.".

It's clear that he sees the frustration fans have had, waiting so long for the next game, and vows that the company is doing what it can to make development on the next title run more smoothly.

Wada's words are very similar to those that came from Rockstar's leadership in the build-up to Grand Theft Auto 6. The 13-year wait for that game was deemed too long, with Phil Hooker, GTA 6's director of development, saying, "The engine, the tools, and the team we've built during this project will allow us to do things more promptly.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm.

In a recent development, if I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech manufacturer and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Manufacturer’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly promptly.

It has been revealed that as it right now stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.".

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that compatible with Switch, Switch 2, and Windows, the GC controller maintains the core shape and layout of the iconic GameCube pad, but adds in a bunch of modern upgrades like TMR sticks and Hall Effect triggers.
  • Colours include purple and orange, which are arguably the most recognisable from the original release (though we're hoping for a Wavebird-inspired silver variant in the future, too).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that 8BitDo, known for its work in providing excellent retro-inspired controllers for modern systems, has confirmed the GC Bluetooth Gamepad to celebrate the GameCube's 25th anniversary. It's presently scheduled to launch on 10th December 2026.

Sources indicate that compatible with Switch, Switch 2, and Windows, the GC controller maintains the core shape and layout of the iconic GameCube pad, but adds in a bunch of modern upgrades like TMR sticks and Hall Effect triggers. Priced at $49.99, it undercuts Nintendo's official offering by $20 and is available for pre-order now.

Colours include purple and orange, which are arguably the most recognisable from the original release (though we're hoping for a Wavebird-inspired silver variant in the future, too). The pad also features single-rotor rumble to replicate the feel of the original, while a new 'ZL' button – which also features on the official Nintendo GameCube pad for Switch 2 – has been designed to be symmetrical to the 'Z' button on the right.

While we do have a dedicated capture button, there unfortunately doesn't appear to be a 'C' button for chat purposes. It's also not clear at this stage whether the GC controller will have wake-up support for Switch 2, but 8BitDo has generally been pretty good at including this, even if it's not necessarily supported immediately at launch.

Here's an official list of features from 8BitDo:.

- Classic GC design and iconic button layout - TMR joysticks with octagonal gates - Hall Effect linear triggers - Single-rotor rumble - Symmetrical Z and ZL bumpers - Capture button for screenshots and recording - Turbo function - Support for multiple simultaneous gamepad connections.

Finally, it's worth noting that if you purchase the 8BitDo Retro Receiver for GC, you can use the latest controller – or indeed the official GameCube pad – with original hardware.

In a recent development, we'll have a review of the 8BitDo GC Bluetooth Gamepad in due course, but what do you make of it so far? Let us know with a comment in the usual place.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've said it before, and I'll say it again; Lego Rivendell is, in my opinion, one of (if not the) best Lego sets around. Even with more modern rivals like Minas Tirith or Barad-dur, I don't think any of them manage to blend spectacle with diorama-style interiors as well as this kit does.

Recent findings suggest that modelled after the elven refuge as it appears in Fellowship of the Ring, this kit is a sprawling recreation of the Last Homely House; with over 6,000 pieces to play with, it can create a level of depth and detail most kits can't hope to match. This is the kind of Lego set where you'll discover something new every time you stop to admire it. Lego Rivendell is also impressive enough on display that it'll draw a "woah" worthy of Owen Wilson from most onlookers.

This model often enjoys a price cut in time for the annual Lego Black Friday deals, but this time it's been given an even bigger saving. Actually, it's dropped to an all-time low price that we haven't seen before. Usually, the best we can expect is a reduction down to £365.

According to recent reports, there are four distinct areas for Lego Rivendell; the main house with its tower and display showing off the broken shards of Narsil, the council area with its ring of seats and plinth for the One Ring, a bridge leading to Arwen's pergola, and a woodland smithy where the elves are busy creating masterworks at the forge. Many of these have a mix of exposed and hidden areas you can reveal by lifting off the lid, which really sells the dollhouse-like experience here.

Industry observers note that the top half of the tower can be removed to show the room where Bilbo Baggins is staying, for instance, and there's a desk set up where he's writing in his memoirs. (Yes, his minifigure has an alternate face so you can recreate that moment as well - shudder). Meanwhile, Arwen's pergola is removable so that you can get a good look at the forge beneath. Oh, and as for the council area? Well, let's just say Sauron's eye is firmly fixed on this meeting...

According to recent reports, then there are the minifigures. Premium Lego sets like this often come with a lot of figs, but Rivendell feels particularly generous. There are 15 in total; Frodo, Sam, Merry, Pippin, Gandalf, Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli, Boromir, Elrond, Arwen, Bilbo, a couple of elves, and a visiting dwarf. That's enough to make the whole kit feel positively alive, and you can recreate a whole host of moments from the movie if you'd like.

I shouldn't skip over the fact that it's downright beautiful to look at, either. Whether it's the tasteful pastel tiles, the abundance of flora carpeting the grounds, or the autumnal trees looming over it all, Lego Rivendell is an incredibly handsome centerpiece.

It looks like the majority of Lego Lord of the Rings kits are on offer right now; the Balrog Book Nook, Sauron's Helmet, Barad-dur, and Minas Tirith have all been heavily reduced in price at Amazon.

Even with the arrival of Lego Minas Tirith earlier this year (which just got its first discount, by the way), I still don't think Rivendell has been surpassed. Yes, the Gondorian city is jaw-dropping. For one thing, it's very cleverly designed with a forced perspective using multiple scales. For another, it's striking in a way Rivendell isn't; a mass of white walls and towers surround the spur of a mountain, drawing every eye in the room. However (and this is no insult to Minas Tirith - I'm at the moment in the middle of building it), I still think Rivendell is prettier and has more 'going on' under the surface.

Basically, I'd always point to this kit if someone asked me what I thought the best ever Lego set was - it's captured both my heart and my imagination, just like its inspiration did when I first saw it on-screen in 2001.

In terms of other Lego news, it looks like there will be 10 Lego Star Wars concept art minifigures for the 50th anniversary.

In a recent development, I've been writing about games in one form or another since 2012, but these days you'll find me managing GamesRadar+'s tabletop gaming and toy coverage (I spend my time here handling everything from board game reviews to the latest Lego news). I've also been obsessed with Warhammer since the 1990s, and love nothing more than running tabletop RPGs like D&D as a Dungeon Master.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some massive news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of newly introduced content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

According to recent reports, as part of this fresh upgrade, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her massive gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Sources indicate that beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

Recent findings suggest that this upgrade will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no fresh characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. The previously promised social space will be coming with this upgrade too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the new runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

Industry observers note that what will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few newly introduced weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, major ole alien enemies to take on.

Recent findings suggest that you've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is currently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you've just started GTA 6 you might be wondering where the nearest airplane and helicopter are located to your starting point.
  • Luckily, there's a reliable spot to snag your first few aircraft close to your starting safehouse, and you can probably steal them without raising a single alarm.
  • You'll drive about 2.5 miles southwest from Jason's house in Key Lento.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you've just started GTA 6 you might be wondering where the nearest airplane and helicopter are located to your starting point. There's a huge latest world to explore, and the best way to do it is by air. But first, you've got to find a plane or chopper to steal.

Luckily, there's a reliable spot to snag your first few aircraft close to your starting safehouse, and you can probably steal them without raising a single alarm.

You'll drive about 2.5 miles southwest from Jason's house in Key Lento. Start the trip by driving southwest through Key Lento, then west through Abismo Key, and finally west and then north to Southwind.

You'll be taking Sunbelt Highway (Route 1) the whole way and you'll know you're close after you cross two long bridges. Southwind is a small district located next to the Mile Zero Air Station: GTA 6's military base.

(Yes, the military base has planes and helicopters too, but it's a little trickier getting your hands on them so check out our GTA 6 military base guide before you attempt it.).

Industry observers note that the highway will make a bend to the north as you enter Southwind. On your right you'll see a concrete barrier alongside the road, and where it ends is where you want to turn right into the parking lot, at the sign for SBW (Sherwin Boatworks) and Chicki's Tiki Bar.

If you're facing the water (east), on your right (to the south) is a small hangar with (typically) a few Mammoth Dodo seaplanes parked inside and around it, and often a couple more moored off the dock. Seaplanes aren't the fastest planes in the game, but they're perfect for early exploration because they can land on both water and land, and they require almost no room to get airborne.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has been revealed that there's never anyone hanging around here, either, so you won't draw any attention if you help yourself to one of these planes. Just drive one into the water and take off, or steal one from the dock.

Recent findings suggest that follow the same instructions to Southwind as above, but instead of looking to the south, look straight east from the entrance to the parking lot. There's an open gate leading out to a dock where a Buckingham Maverick helicopter is sitting.

Just ignore the no trespassing sign, run over to the dock, and hop into it. Now the skies are yours.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey?
  • IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business concerns they may face as a result.
  • Zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain organization finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are right now technically and legally preparing themselves.

IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business concerns they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.".

Zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he said.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.".

Essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer says the games industry "is eating itself" amid mass layoffs

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's writer and Sandfall Interactive's former narrative lead, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, thinks the game industry is "eating itself" and "losing so much institutional knowledge" through mass layoffs and studio closures.
  • A lot of what's happening really breaks my heart.
  • In a recent development, "I come from an investment background.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's writer and Sandfall Interactive's former narrative lead, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, thinks the game industry is "eating itself" and "losing so much institutional knowledge" through mass layoffs and studio closures.

"I look around the game industry. A lot of what's happening really breaks my heart. I feel that the industry is eating itself. I feel that we are losing so much institutional knowledge. We're making it extraordinarily difficult for a younger generation of developers to have formative experiences. There's so much disruption in the industry right now," she says in an interview with GamesBeat.

In a recent development, "I come from an investment background. My original background was in private equity. I've seen that side. It frustrates me, because I think about it as, to use an agricultural analogy – in the past we've over-harvested the soil. We've tried to extract everything we can from the land. What we really need to do is cultivate the land. We need stewardship over the land. That means not over-harvesting. That means reinvesting in the land, in making sure there are nutrients put back into the land, so we can grow bigger and better things. I feel that we are not doing that as an industry," she adds.

It has been revealed that svedberg-Yen's not content with watching the chaos unfold, though. The award-winning writer is now working to set up a narrative investment fund to help developers along "between the seed stage and going to publishers." As she explains, many smaller creators need to develop a demo before pitching their games to publishers. "But to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers." Her investment fund will hopefully help devs crack the "chicken and egg question," and minimize risk at the earliest stages of production.

"I'm not trying to compete with publishers," she says. "But I'm trying to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make.".

Svedberg-Yen's comments come during a devastating year for the games industry. Xbox plans to reduce its headcount by 3,200 by next summer. Sony shuttered Bluepoint Games and made layoffs at Sucker Punch. EA closed BioWare after a whopping three-decade run. Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics laid off workers for the sixth time since its last full game. Even the most acclaimed developers are still at risk, and keeping track of all the layoffs in 2026 alone would likely require a dedicated Excel sheet.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has sold 8.7 million copies and made $366 million, analyst indicates, and that's despite the "Game Pass cannibalization.".

GTA games have often had women on their box arts, but it's vital to note this doesn't necessarily mean they'll play an important role in the story — or even appear at all. History has taught us the girls on the front cover can sometimes appear in minor roles within the plot, but they're usually not critical to the story.

In a recent development, for example, the cover girl from GTA 5, the girl taking a picture in a red bikini, doesn't appear in the game whatsoever. It is the same for GTA 4: the girl wearing a red top and licking a lollipop isn't in the game. In fact, in terms of the mainline entries, you'd need to go back to Vice City for an example of the cover girl actually being in the game.

As such, there's a chance the GTA 6 cover girl is purely for promotional purposes — she might not be in the game at all.

Industry observers note that so, there's a fairly good chance the GTA 6 cover girl won't be in the game itself, but is she based on a real person? While developer Rockstar hasn't mentioned yet, the Internet believes it's found someone with a very, very strong resemblance.

Gabriela Chiquin, who is an influencer, DJ, and musician from Venezuela, looks a lot like the GTA 6 cover girl. In a number of Instagram posts, she has her hair curled similarly to the cover girl, and wears green clothing. The pictures of her in green are from a few years ago, so they weren't taken in response to the attention she's gotten from the link to GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that having caught wind of the similarities, she said in an Instagram post: "I want to thank the entire GTA community for so much love. I never imagined receiving so many messages, comments, and memes." She doesn't actually say whether she is the GTA 6 cover girl or not, however.

The cover girls for its game isn't something Rockstar usually makes a massive deal out of, so it's unlikely we'll ever get official confirmation that Chiquin is the actual inspiration for the GTA 6 cover girl. Still, there's a very clear resemblance here, and the Internet managed to make the connection within days.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring upcoming creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

Industry observers note that sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

It has been revealed that for those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was declared back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a upcoming name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I recruited the biggest Star Trek fan I know to help me road test the new Magic: The Gathering set. Right away he was impressed by cards that referenced the Star Trek: Prodigy cartoon and Star Trek Beyond—a third movie in the J. J. Abrams-verse I completely forgot was even made—but if that kind of trainspotting was all it took to make a successful crossover then people would have liked the Spider-Man cards a lot more than they did.

What makes the better Universes Beyond crossovers work is how they bring out the themes of their source material, turning motifs into mechanics that make a set feel like a genuine expression of the thing being adapted rather than just another property being fed into the content machine. Having played some games with the cards, yeah, I think Star Trek works.

It has been revealed that I built a blue-green deck around Strange New Worlds, a mechanic that rewards you for having different lands rather than just stacking Islands and Forests. When I played Deep Space Scan I drew a card for each differently named land I had, and those lands also lowered the cost of powering up my Astute Terraformer.

Meanwhile, the Federation mechanic gives bonuses for having different creature types on the table like Vulcan and Klingon and Romulan (though not Borg). With just those two mechanics, the set emphasizes exploration and diversity. You really do want to put together a crew representing multiple species and send them into the final frontier. (There is of course a card called Final Frontier.).

According to recent reports, star Trek also makes use of the spacecraft mechanics introduced in Edge of Eternities, where a ship starts with limited capabilities but has to be stationed by tapping creatures to add charge counters to access its full abilities—like flying and fighting. Lt. Cmdr. Geordi La Forge is a solid combo, doubling the amount of charge counters you add each time and letting you get the Enterprise into the air twice as fast.

Recent findings suggest that there are cards for various different iterations of the Enterprise, but I'm partial to U.S.S. Enterprise-A, Free Spirit, because when you play it you get three red 1/1 officer tokens for free. That makes it faster to station, and after that you've got three disposable officers to chump block with. Which is why they're red.

Industry observers note that there's also a Beam Me Up mechanic to bring a card back from the discard pile at the cost of returning a card from the table to your hand, and a cute assimilate mechanic that lets you wipe creatures' existing types then turn them into artifacts under your control for your Borg deck. But what makes the Star Trek cards feel like Star Trek is how much they emphasize teamwork.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

According to recent reports, the Common Goal card lets two creatures deal damage together, and there's a whole suite of cards that get better when you've got creatures with a total power of 8 attacking as one. Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior, who doubles his own power when he's part of that attack, proved a gamewinner for my red/white deck more than once. The thing that really comes across is Star Trek's utopian ideal of everyone pulling together in a crisis and being better for our differences. It's optimistic, with stars in its eyes, and even a casual Star Trek watcher like me can appreciate that.

Magic: The Gathering's Star Trek set is available now, for both tabletop Magic and Arena.

Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

According to recent reports, I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was declared in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

When it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

There are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Valve has released a upcoming Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.
  • As per Valve's announcement post, average framerates are now listed in the Steam Deck Compatibility section of a game's store page, but you'll need to click Learn More to see it.
  • According to recent reports, according to Valve, average framerates are derived from players running the game on their Steam Decks, assuming they've opted in to provide framerate data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valve has released a upcoming Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

As per Valve's announcement post, average framerates are now listed in the Steam Deck Compatibility section of a game's store page, but you'll need to click Learn More to see it. Additionally, the feature is only available for games that have been tested for Deck compatibility - those with Verified, Playable, or Unsupported badges - so while it's not a complete list, it still covers thousands of titles.

According to recent reports, according to Valve, average framerates are derived from players running the game on their Steam Decks, assuming they've opted in to provide framerate data. And the store widget also includes another helpful addition: a histogram displaying the percentage of data samples. This reveals how often a particular framerate has been reported, and is useful in determining if the game's framerate is sporadic, such as due to stutters.

"The current Steam Deck Verified compatibility rating is based on standardised test criteria, but it may not match every customer's bar for acceptable gameplay," Valve explained of the fresh feature.

In a recent development, "This is especially true around performance - a game with an Unsupported rating due to unstable performance may be considered playable by some customers, and a Verified game may not reach a framerate that some customers prefer to play at. By providing average framerate data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture of how the game performs on Steam Deck and can make more informed purchase and play decisions.".

Industry observers note that at the moment, Steam's framerate data feature only covers performance on Steam Deck, and for a very good reason: Valve's handheld has standardised hardware, so the results will be the same for all players. However, Valve notes it intends to provide framerate data for more devices in the future, but it's not clear if that's ever going to include desktop PCs, considering the complex nature of their hardware configurations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major revision, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

It has been revealed that first off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The fresh patch continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

In a recent development, the significant inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Recent findings suggest that evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

According to recent reports, you may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a fresh weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

Recent findings suggest that it can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

It has been revealed that as part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Industry observers note that currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding latest decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Industry observers note that elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 releases and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

Tom Hiddleston has revealed the call from Marvel bosses that proved to him how integral Loki was to Avengers: Doomsday.

It has been revealed that "The call came from [Marvel Studios president] Kevin Feige and [co-president] Louis D'Esposito, and it was very clear there was no way of continuing a story about the multiverse without Loki," Hiddleston told Empire magazine. "They wanted me to be part of it. That's what they stated.".

Hiddleston also mentioned that the multiverse – a narrative concept now reaching critical mass thanks to the MCU – and Loki are effectively intertwined at this point, making the notion of ignoring the former trickster god all but impossible.

Hiddleston said, "At this point, having expanded what we can call the multiverse in a way that isn't a niche reference now, and Loki's position as the God of Stories, on the big chair at the End of Time, holding the branches of many timelines together, there was no way to continue to talk about the multiverse without acknowledging his position.".

Away from Doomsday, the newfound God of Stories has also been a crucial component for Marvel's so-called 'Multiverse Saga', a sprawling chapter of MCU movies and demonstrates that kicked off with WandaVision, Falcon and The Winter Soldier, and Loki in 2021, and culminating with Avengers: Secret Wars in 2027.

Loki has largely been at the forefront of the more multiverse-heavy adventures, inadvertently splintering the multiverse in Loki season 1, before acting as the force to hold them together in Loki season 2.

Loki also doorstepped Peggy Carter and Steve Rogers just after their iconic dance in Avengers: Endgame – as revealed during the fresh ending of Endgame's Encore re-release.

Of course, Loki isn't the only notable Marvel figure rocking up in Avengers: Doomsday. Far from it. Alongside him is Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, Steve Rogers, plus the casts of Fantastic Four and Thunderbolts. Several OG Avengers are also on the scene, plus multiple members of Fox's X-Men team, including Professor X, Magneto, and Cyclops.

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and US cinemas on December 18.

For more, we've done our best TVA impression and untangled the Marvel timeline for you.
